macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street rebounds as semiconductors offset Middle East jitters
items.summary: US stocks recovered, with semiconductor strength helping offset concern over renewed tensions in the Middle East. MarketScreener also showed the Nasdaq 100 up 1.60% and the S&P 500 up 0.75%, while Brent crude fell 4.01%.

items.title: Investors refocus on Fed, BOE and BOJ as central banks face a decisive week
items.summary: Markets are watching a busy week of central bank meetings, including the Federal Reserve, the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan. XTB said the consensus does not expect rate changes, but expects cautious messaging that keeps the door open to future hikes if inflation does not ease.

items.title: Wall Street and oil swing on renewed Middle East conflict concerns
items.summary: Recent market coverage says US equities moved higher while oil fell as investors assessed the resumption of conflict in the Middle East. Bloomberg Línea also noted that oil had recently approached US$80 amid Iran-related tensions before risk appetite improved.

items.title: US employment data weighs on the Ibex 35
items.summary: Expansion reported that the Spanish Ibex fell below 18,100 points after a US jobs release. The move highlights how fresh US macro data is influencing European equities and rate expectations.

items.title: Orange beats earnings expectations and lifts guidance, boosting shares
items.summary: Orange rose 2.2% after reporting record first-half growth, with revenue up 3.5% year over year to 20.9 billion euros and EBITDAaL up 5.0% to 6.1 billion euros. The company also announced a 50/50 data-center joint venture with Morrison backed by a 3 billion-euro investment plan.

items.title: Bank of America plans to redeem $2.6 billion in senior debt
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that Bank of America will amortize 2.6 billion dollars in senior bonds, a capital-management move that may attract investor attention in financials.

items.title: Paul Grewal leaves Coinbase as chief legal officer
items.summary: MarketScreener said Coinbase’s legal chief Paul Grewal has stepped down with immediate effect. The departure adds another notable corporate headline in the crypto sector.

items.title: Meta reportedly plans AI chip production to start in September
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that Meta Platforms expects to begin producing AI chips in September to expand its computing capacity. The announcement underscores continued heavy investment in AI infrastructure.

items.title: AstraZeneca wins patent battle against Pfizer over cancer drug
items.summary: MarketScreener highlighted a court victory for AstraZeneca in a patent dispute with Pfizer tied to a cancer treatment. The case is an important legal development for large-cap healthcare names.

items.title: Analysts flag sharp swings in Asian and European markets
items.summary: Coverage from XTB said Asian equities saw heavy losses led by semiconductors, with Korea’s KOSPI at one point down more than 10% and Japan’s Nikkei off 4.3%, while European markets benefited from lower oil and reduced geopolitical risk. That backdrop helped explain the mixed tone across global indices.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum rally as geopolitical tensions ease
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed to about $65,229, while Ethereum rose to around $1,944, as easing U.S.-Iran tensions improved risk sentiment across crypto markets. The broader crypto market cap also increased to roughly $2.23 trillion.

items.title: BitMart shuts down after nine years, BMX token plunges
items.summary: Centralized exchange BitMart reportedly shut down after nine years of operation, sending its BMX token down 58%. The move highlights ongoing exchange risk and token vulnerability in the market.

items.title: Bitcoin recovers above $63,000 as risk appetite improves
items.summary: Bitcoin rose above $63,000 as lower oil prices and improved risk appetite supported crypto demand. Market commentary said easing geopolitical pressure helped lift sentiment.

items.title: XRP gains as SWIFT-linked bank activity boosts payment narrative
items.summary: XRP advanced after reports that SWIFT tapped Ripple-linked banks for blockchain payments. The development added attention to blockchain-based cross-border settlement use cases.

items.title: Hong Kong tightens crypto platform authentication requirements
items.summary: The Hong Kong SFC forced crypto platforms to stop using SMS authentication, reflecting continued regulatory tightening around exchange security and user protection. The rule adds to compliance pressure on regional platforms.

items.title: Bank of Korea defends bank-first stablecoin approach
items.summary: South Korea’s central bank defended its bank-first stablecoin framework amid legislative deadlock. The policy debate underscores how stablecoin regulation remains unsettled in major Asian markets.

items.title: Paul Grewal exits Coinbase legal leadership ahead of CLARITY vote
items.summary: Coinbase’s legal chief Paul Grewal exited his role before a critical CLARITY Act vote, drawing attention to the policy backdrop facing U.S. crypto firms. The timing adds to uncertainty around pending U.S. regulation.

items.title: PayPal expands PYUSD stablecoin to Polygon’s Open Money Stack
items.summary: PayPal brought its PYUSD stablecoin to Polygon’s Open Money Stack, signaling continued product expansion for one of the most prominent corporate stablecoin initiatives. The move strengthens stablecoin integration with blockchain payment infrastructure.

items.title: Robinhood Chain draws DeFi attention as Uniswap volume surges
items.summary: Robinhood Chain sparked interest in DeFi while Uniswap volume reportedly hit $500 million in eight days. The activity suggests renewed experimentation around onchain trading and retail-facing DeFi infrastructure.

items.title: INTERPOL operation blocks illicit crypto transfers and arrests thousands
items.summary: INTERPOL said an operation blocked illicit crypto transfers and led to 5,811 arrests. The enforcement action highlights continued international focus on crypto-related financial crime.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across different applications and files, extending its push into professional AI tools. Reuters also reports the launch is part of intensifying competition with other enterprise AI offerings.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark developer access and upgraded model
items.summary: Meta released long-awaited developer access to its Muse Spark AI model, along with an upgraded version, in a move aimed at competing more directly in the paid AI model market. Reuters says the release pits Meta against Anthropic and OpenAI on monetization strategy.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live, a real-time voice model family
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release expands OpenAI’s multimodal and conversational AI offerings.

items.title: SpaceXAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI launched the Grok 4.5 model, describing it as its most intelligent model to date and optimized for coding and agentic tasks. The launch adds another major model release to the fast-moving frontier of foundation-model competition.

items.title: Meta plans to begin manufacturing an AI chip in September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to start manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip from September, as part of a broader effort to expand computing power. The memo cited by Reuters also ties the plan to Meta’s large-scale data and infrastructure buildout.

items.title: Micron plans more than $250 billion in U.S. investment through 2035
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest more than $250 billion in the United States through 2035, citing surging memory-chip demand from AI. Reuters framed the announcement as part of the ongoing AI infrastructure and semiconductor expansion.

items.title: Meta announces first Canadian data center in Alberta
items.summary: Meta said it will build a massive data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada. Reuters says the facility is part of the company’s effort to rapidly expand compute capacity for AI workloads.

items.title: Anthropic appoints Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic said it appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body charged with ensuring the company remains committed to its public mission. The move underscores continued governance and safety-focused experimentation among leading AI firms.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony confirms end of physical PlayStation game discs starting in 2028
items.summary: Sony Interactive Entertainment said new PlayStation games will stop using physical discs from January 2028, marking a major shift toward digital-only distribution. The move has become one of the biggest industry stories of the day.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly sells off four Xbox studios amid major gaming restructuring
items.summary: Microsoft is said to be divesting four Xbox studios while also cutting roughly 1,600 jobs in its gaming division. The reported overhaul is one of the most significant industry developments in the latest cycle of gaming news.

items.title: Capcom moves up Onimusha: Way of the Sword release date
items.summary: Capcom has reportedly advanced the launch of Onimusha: Way of the Sword to September 4, earlier than the previously planned September 25 date. The change is a notable release update for one of Capcom’s upcoming games.

items.title: Nintendo will shut down Mario Kart Tour this September
items.summary: Nintendo has announced that Mario Kart Tour will be discontinued in September after seven years of service. The shutdown is a notable end-of-life move for one of Nintendo’s mobile games.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass growth falls short of Microsoft’s expectations
items.summary: Xbox leadership has acknowledged that Game Pass has not grown as quickly as Microsoft had projected, with reports suggesting it remains tens of millions of subscribers below earlier targets. The comments add to broader scrutiny of Microsoft’s gaming strategy.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports arrive on PS5
items.summary: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and Black Ops 2 are now available on PS4 and PS5, bringing two classic entries to current PlayStation hardware. The release is notable, though reports say it comes at a relatively high price.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced posts strong Steam launch
items.summary: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced has reportedly reached around 100,000 concurrent players on Steam, the highest peak yet for an Assassin’s Creed title. The launch suggests strong renewed interest in the series.

items.title: Pokemon Go marks 10th anniversary with live event coverage
items.summary: Pokemon Go held a 10th anniversary livestream featuring new announcements and surprises for players. The event stands out as one of the day’s biggest live-service game updates.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Swift launches blockchain-based shared ledger with 16 banks
items.summary: Swift introduced a blockchain-based shared ledger aimed at enabling round-the-clock cross-border payments and competing with stablecoin-based systems. The initial network includes 16 banks such as Citi and HSBC.

items.title: India scraps import duties on some mobile phone and electronics parts
items.summary: India removed 7.5% and 5% import levies on selected components used to make mobile phones and other electronics. The move is intended to support manufacturers such as Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: Apple to spend over $30 billion in Broadcom chip-supply deal
items.summary: Apple said it will spend more than $30 billion under a chip-supply agreement with Broadcom. Broadcom will also expand a factory in Colorado as part of the deal.

items.title: Meta begins in-house design of new smart glasses
items.summary: Meta announced a new line of smart glasses designed in-house, signaling a deeper push into wearables. The company is positioning the products as part of its broader hardware strategy.

items.title: Microsoft cuts nearly 5,000 workers, heavily in Xbox
items.summary: Microsoft is laying off about 5,000 workers, with a large share coming from its Xbox division. The company says the restructuring is meant to refocus the business and redirect resources.

items.title: Apple raises prices on some Macs and iPads
items.summary: Apple increased prices on some of its MacBook and iPad models. The company cited higher memory and storage chip costs tied to the broader semiconductor supply environment.

items.title: South Korean chipmakers plan $518 billion manufacturing hub
items.summary: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are planning a massive new chipmaking hub in South Korea. The investment is intended to serve rising global semiconductor demand.

items.title: EU moves to protect steel industry and limit small e-commerce parcels
items.summary: The European Union introduced two measures affecting trade and e-commerce, including steps to protect the steel sector and limit small parcel flows. The changes could affect technology-linked retail and logistics operations.
